title: 📘 UNIT 8: GEOSPATIAL INFORMATION AND DATA PROCESSING
notes: 🌍 Geospatial information and data processing → the collection, processing, analysis, representation, and use of geographic data.

title: 8.1 📍 BASIC CONCEPTS OF GEOSPATIAL INFORMATION
notes:
📊 Data → collected observations represented as numbers, characters, images, facts, or symbols.

💡 Information → processed and organized data that has meaning and adds knowledge.

📍 Geospatial data → data about objects, events, or phenomena that have a location on Earth's surface.

🗺️ Geographic data → connects place, time, and attributes and forms the basis of mapmaking.

📌 Location information → identifies where a geographic feature exists, usually using coordinates.

⏱️ Temporal information → identifies the time when a location and its attributes existed.

🏷️ Attribute information → describes characteristics of mapped features, such as temperature, elevation, population, or income.

🔑 Geospatial data = Location + Attributes + Time.

title: 8.1.1 📊 DATA AND INFORMATION
notes:
📥 Data → unprocessed facts or figures used as input.

📤 Information → processed data used as output.

🔄 Data lifecycle → Collection → Processing → Analysis → Dissemination.

1️⃣ Collection → gathering primary or secondary data.

2️⃣ Processing → checking quality, correcting, merging, and organizing data.

3️⃣ Analysis → examining data to identify relationships and meaningful patterns.

4️⃣ Dissemination → sharing results through reports, conferences, workshops, publications, or other forms.

title: 8.1.2 🗺️ VISUALIZING GEOGRAPHIC DATA
notes:
📌 Discrete objects → geographic features with clearly defined boundaries.

🏞️ Example → a lake.

🌡️ Continuous data → phenomena that gradually vary across a surface.

⛰️ Example → elevation or temperature.

🔑 Difference → Discrete data has identifiable boundaries; continuous data varies across space.

title: 8.2 🛰️ SOURCES AND TOOLS OF GEOGRAPHIC DATA
notes:
📚 Geographic data sources → directly collected data and remotely sensed data.

👨‍🔬 Directly collected data → gathered at the location where the phenomenon is measured.

📌 Examples → weather-station measurements, field surveys, census, sample surveys, and direct observation.

🛰️ Remotely sensed data → collected from a distance without direct physical contact with the feature.

📡 Examples → satellite images and aerial photographs.

🗂️ Common sources → hard-copy maps, aerial photographs, remotely sensed imagery, survey samples, and existing digital data.

title: 8.2.1 🧭 TOOLS FOR GEOGRAPHIC DATA COLLECTION
notes:
🧭 Field survey → systematic observation, measurement, and recording of geographic information in an area.

📍 GPS (Global Positioning System) → satellite-based system used to determine the precise location of a place.

🛰️ GPS → provides latitude, longitude, and elevation information.

💻 Digitizer → converts information from analogue or paper form into digital, computer-readable form.

📱 Digitization tools → table digitizers, scanners, and smartphones.

🌐 Georeferencing → relating an image or map's internal coordinates to a geographic coordinate system.

📚 Primary sources → data collected directly for a particular purpose.

📖 Secondary sources → existing data collected previously for other purposes and reused.

title: 8.3 🗺️ GEOGRAPHIC DATA REPRESENTATIONS
notes:
🗺️ Geographic data representation → graphical visualization of geographic information or production of maps.

📄 Analogue format → geographic information represented on physical materials such as paper maps.

💻 Digital format → geographic information represented electronically and processed by computers.

⚡ Advantages of digital data → easy to copy, transmit, store, transform, process, and analyze.

📌 Basic map features → Point, Line, and Area (Polygon).

📍 Point → represents a feature at a single location, such as a weather station or water well.

〰️ Line → represents a feature using connected coordinates, such as rivers, roads, or pipelines.

🔷 Polygon/Area → represents a feature enclosed by connected coordinates, such as forests, soil areas, administrative boundaries, and climate zones.

title: 8.3.1 💻 DIGITAL SPATIAL DATA MODELS
notes:
🔷 Vector data → represents geographic features using points, lines, and polygons defined by coordinates.

📍 Point vector → one coordinate pair.

〰️ Line vector → sequence of connected vertices; lines may end at nodes.

🔷 Polygon vector → closed set of coordinate pairs representing an area.

🟩 Raster data → represents geographic space as a grid of cells arranged in rows and columns.

📐 Raster → points are represented by single cells, lines by neighboring cells, and areas by groups of connected cells.

🖼️ Image data → represents geographic landscapes through pictures or photographs.

🔑 Vector = coordinates/features; Raster = grid cells.

title: 8.4 🗺️ ADVANCES IN MAPMAKING AND GIS
notes:
🗺️ Mapmaking → the graphical representation of the Earth's surface and geographic information.

📜 Historical development → maps developed from early simple and distorted representations into increasingly accurate maps.

🔭 Major advances → mathematics, astronomy, latitude and longitude, printing, photography, aircraft, and satellites.

🛰️ Satellites → provide detailed and frequently updated information over large areas of Earth.

💻 GIS (Geographic Information System) → a computer-based system used to store, visualize, analyze, and interpret geographic data.

title: 8.4.1 🧩 COMPONENTS OF GIS
notes:
🖥️ Hardware → computers and devices such as printers, scanners, and plotters used to operate GIS.

💻 Software → programs used to store, analyze, and display geographic information.

👥 People → administrators, managers, GIS technicians, application experts, end users, and consumers.

📋 Methods → guidelines, specifications, standards, procedures, and plans for applying GIS.

🗂️ Data → accurate geographic information used by GIS, including vector, raster, image, and attribute data.

🔑 GIS components → Hardware + Software + People + Methods + Data.

title: 8.4.2 🗺️ CREATING A LOCAL ADMINISTRATIVE MAP
notes:
🗂️ Basic process → obtain geographic data → add data layers → select the area of interest → edit/display layers → export the selected data → prepare the map layout.

🇪🇹 Example → creating an administrative map of Oromia National Regional State using geographic data/shapefiles.

📌 Map marginal information → Legend, Scale bar, North arrow, Coordinate information, Gridlines, and Date of map compilation.

title: 8.5 📊 MAKING AND INTERPRETATION OF GRAPHS, CHARTS AND DIAGRAMS
notes:
📊 Graphs, charts, and diagrams → present data clearly, show trends, make comparisons, and explain relationships.

💻 Common tools → Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Word, and statistical/spreadsheet software.

📊 Bar graph → compares independent data series; bar height or length represents value or frequency.

📈 Line graph → shows how data changes over time and is useful for identifying trends.

🥧 Pie chart → shows how a whole is divided into categories or percentages.

🔗 Diagram → illustrates how different parts or components are connected, related, or overlap.

title: 📚 UNIT 8 SUMMARY
notes:
📍 Geospatial data → geographic information connected to location and attributes, often with time.

📊 Data → raw observations; Information → processed data with meaning.

🛰️ Geographic data → collected directly through surveys and observations or remotely through satellites and aerial photography.

🧭 GPS → determines geographic location using satellites.

💻 Digitizer → converts analogue information into digital form.

🗺️ Geographic features → represented as points, lines, and polygons.

🔷 Vector → coordinate-based representation; 🟩 Raster → grid-cell representation.

💻 GIS → stores, visualizes, analyzes, and interprets geographic data.

📊 Graphs and charts → make geographic data easier to compare, interpret, and communicate.

title: 📝 UNIT 8: EXAM QUICK REVIEW
notes:
🔹 Data = unprocessed facts or observations.

🔹 Information = processed data with meaning.

🔹 Geospatial data = data connected to a geographic location.

🔹 Geospatial elements = Location + Attributes + Time.

🔹 Discrete = clearly defined boundaries.

🔹 Continuous = values gradually vary across space.

🔹 Direct data = collected at the source.

🔹 Remote sensing = data collected from a distance.

🔹 GPS = determines location using satellites.

🔹 Digitizer = converts analogue information into digital form.

🔹 Point = single location.

🔹 Line = connected coordinates.

🔹 Polygon = closed area.

🔹 Vector = points, lines, and polygons using coordinates.

🔹 Raster = grid cells.

🔹 GIS = computer system for storing, visualizing, analyzing, and interpreting geographic data.

🔹 Line graph = change over time.

🔹 Pie chart = parts of a whole.

🔹 Diagram = relationships between components.
